mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a relative housing rebound, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 response over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with sector rotation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) rises above its 12-month moving average signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher corporate margins.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS exceed their 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO below its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index above 0.4% signals an acceleration in inflation, which historically precedes a positive S&P 500 response over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate preemptive rate hikes that boost financial sector returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.4% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in the unemployment rate above 6% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% in a given month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based expansion in supply capacity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.
